- [2023/07/22] The user inquired about how gravity works according to modern physics.
- [2023/07/22] The assistant explained that gravity is a fundamental force described by Einstein's theory of general relativity, which states that mass and energy warp spacetime, causing objects to be attracted towards each other.
- [2023/07/22] The user asked about Newton’s definition of gravity.
- [2023/07/22] The assistant provided information on Newton's law of universal gravitation, which defines gravity as a force proportional to the product of masses and inversely proportional to the square of distance between them.
- [2023/07/22] The user requested a comparison between Newton’s and Einstein’s theories of gravity.
- [2023/07/22] The assistant explained that while Newton's law describes gravity as an instantaneous force, Einstein's theory describes it as spacetime curvature caused by mass and energy, explaining phenomena like Mercury's orbit deviation and gravitational lensing.
- [2023/07/22] The user asked if all particles of the Earth attract objects towards its center according to Newton’s law.
- [2023/07/22] The assistant confirmed that in Newtonian physics, every particle with mass contributes to the gravitational pull on an object toward the Earth's center.
- [2023/07/22] The user questioned how a surface-near particle of the Earth still attracts objects towards the center despite being closer to the surface than the center.
- [2023/07/22] The assistant clarified that even particles near the surface contribute to the overall gravitational force, as their mass and distance from an object influence the net gravitational pull toward the Earth's center.
